minutes.headline: Stormwater Task Force will merge two outreach decks and firm up fee numbers before briefing town boards.
minutes.summary: The task force mostly discussed its outreach presentation for creating a stormwater utility: merging the consultant's deck with a member's own, pinning down fee numbers, and which boards to brief first. Members also reviewed recent drainage repairs, MS4 compliance gaps, and missing meeting minutes. Two sets of minutes were approved and the next meeting was set.

attendees.role: land use director, discussed but not present

budget_items.topic: Detention basin cleanout, Flat Hill village
budget_items.what_was_said: The town gave money for a contractor to clean out the basin; the trustees reportedly paid for the rest including the outlet structure.
ARPA money was committed last year and the invoice was still needed so the money can be spent.
Members recalled a per-household annual figure being discussed, with large commercial properties paying more.

budget_items.topic: Fee as a share of a household bill
budget_items.what_was_said: Members debated whether the annual fee amounts to roughly one percent or half a percent and what is sellable to the public.

budget_items.topic: Cost of engineering and design for projects
budget_items.what_was_said: A member suggested documenting the process and the range of cost depending on scope, since projects are vague.

budget_items.topic: Consultant revenue goal and fee structures
budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant's deck reportedly assumed a revenue goal and several funding models, including a tiered commercial structure.
A member recalled the plan included an engineer, billing staff and a maintenance equipment operator.
The town is not meeting catch basin cleaning and sweeping requirements for lack of staff or funds, and could face substantial fines.

decisions.decision: A member will merge the consultant's deck and his own into one presentation, expected in about two meetings.
Trajectory agreed: pin down numbers with the consultant, brief the finance committee and possibly select board, then advertise and hold public meetings.
Target December for getting on the finance committee agenda, otherwise whatever slot is offered.
Next meeting set for the 17th of October.
A member will talk to Nick about pinning down residential and commercial fee numbers before going to other boards.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed to merge the consultant's outreach deck and a member's own into one presentation, expected in about two meetings.
Members agreed an order of work: pin down fee numbers with the consultant, brief the finance committee and possibly the select board, then advertise and hold public meetings.
A member will talk to the consultant about residential and commercial fee numbers before the task force goes to other boards.
Members noted the town is not meeting catch basin cleaning and sweeping requirements under its MS4 permit and could face substantial fines.
The task force set December as its target for the finance committee agenda and set its next meeting for the 17th of October.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility would put a new recurring charge on household and commercial bills, and the fee amounts and how they are split were still being worked out at this meeting.
The town is described as short of staff or funds to meet its catch basin cleaning and sweeping requirements, which is the problem a utility is meant to pay for.
watch_next: Next task force meeting on the 17th of October.
The merged outreach presentation, and whether the task force gets onto the finance committee agenda in December.
